full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Jalil, J.:- This Rule obtained by the decree-holder petitioner on an application U/S. 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, calls in question an order passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Misc. Case No. 47/74 as order no. 126 dated 6-8-78 directing the decree-holder to proceed with the execution case by determining the location of holding no. 339 i.e. the suit property with further direction not to dispossess the 3rd party opposite party Md. Zakaria from holding no. 339A in execution of the decree passed in Other Suit No. 59/71/50/69. 

 2. The present petitioner obtained a decree for ejectment against Md. Ilias Majhi in Other Suit No.50/69 on contest. That decree was put to execution in Other Execution Case No. 10/73 for eviction of judgment debtor Ilias Majhi. It appears that the decree holder went to take possession through process of the court but could not get possession due to resistance and filed an application to get delivery of possession with the help of the police on the ground of resistance by the judgment debtor and his men. In that pending execution case the present opposite party Md. Zakaria, a 3rd party filed an application under Order 21 Rule 99 and 100 and U/S. 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for not allowing the decree holder to execute the decree without determining the location of holding no.339 on the allegation inter alia, that the decree holder already obtained possession of the suit holding no.339 Madarbari P.S. Doublemoorings. District Chittagong out of Court but now under the garb of the decree he is trying to evict the 3rd party-opposite party from his holding no. 339A and so it is necessary to ascertain the decretal property before issuance of the writ of delivery of possession. It was further contended in that application that Municipal holding no.339A is a separate and distinct holding which is situated in the extreme north of R.S. plot no.1919 intervened by a common passage in between Municipal holding no. 339 and 339A. It was further alleged that the 3rd party opposite party filed a separate suit no. 58/74 in the 2nd Court of the Munsif, Chittagong for permanent injunction. It is admitted by both the parties that the said suit has been decreed against the petitioner by which the petitioner is restrained by perpetual injunction from dispossessing the plaintiffs of that suit (3rd party opposite party) from holding no. 339A, Majhirghat, Chittagong and from disturbing his possession therein and that decree was affirmed by the appellate court in Other Appeal No. 168/706 and we are informed by the petitioner that against the said appellate decree a second appeal is pending but there is no stay order. 

 3. The decree holder contested the said application by filing a written objection denying the material allegations and asserting inter alia, that the provisions of Order 21 Rule 99 and 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure have no application to the present case and that the application was filed malafide and the decree holder has no intention to take possession of holding no. 339A as his decree is directed against holding no.339 only and the 3rd party has no right to file any application in the execution case filed against another person, that is judgment debtor. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the prayer of the 3rd party and passed by impugned order. 

 4. The impugned order as it stands, that is, "O.P.I is directed to proceed with the execution case by determining the location of holding no. 339 as described in the agreement in persuance of which the decree in question was passed. He is further directed not to dispossess the petitioner from holding no. 339A in execution of the decree of other suit 50/69", seems to be harmless as it only directed the decree holder to take possession of the suit property after determining its location, and as the decree holder according to him, does not intend to take possession of any other land, there is no question of causing prejudice to him. 

 5. But a question has arisen in this case as to whether the executing court has jurisdiction to pass such order at the instance of a 3rd party who has no locus standi at this stage. Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate has taken us through the provisions of Order 21 Rules 99 and 100 wherefrom it appears that the executing court may pass such order in case of resistance but that order must be on an application filed by the decree holder under Order 21 Rule 97 of the same Code. The 3rd party cannot file such application but he may file an application if evicted under Rule 100 of the said order and the executing Court may investigate into the matter and restore the applicant in possession. This position of law is also not challenged by Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned advocate appearing for the 3rd party-opposite party; but his case is that his application and the impugned order passed there on are covered by Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure as at the present stage when he has not been dispossessed he cannot take resort to provisions of Order 21 Rule 100 and so section 151 is the only section under which the court may grant appropriate relief under its inherent jurisdiction. He has cited some decisions on that point. The first one is PLD 1959 Lahore 511. In that case (Mst. Sahib-un-nissa and others V. Mst. Mahmooda Begum) a 3rd person who is not a party to the decree applied to the court executing the decree U/S. 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the application was allowed and a single Judge of West Pakistan High Court held that when the party has not yet been dispossessed it is a matter of discretion with the court whether it would or would not determine the question beforehand. Next Mr. Rahman cited a case reported in 25 DLR 5. This case was in connection with a matter U/S. 53A of the Transfer of Property Act which is not applicable to the present case. As against that Mr. M. Fazlul Karim has cited a case reported in 29 DLR (SC) 185 Punjab Ali Pramanik and others V. Mohd. Mokarram Hossain) and submits that where specific relief is available, inherent power of Courts U/S. 151 can not be invoked; the said case arose out of an application for setting aside sale and their lordships were pleased to observe- 

 “Order 21, Rule 90 of the Code, as it stands, empowers a Court, which has held an auction sale, to set aside the sale on an application made, amongst others, by a person whose interests have been affected by the sale, on the ground that there has been material irregularity or fraud in publishing or conducting the said sale. If the ground for impugning the sale is fraud in publishing or conducting the sale then, according to the terms of the rule, the proceeding is to be initiated by a person as has been named in the said rule and recourse cannot, certainly, be taken to section 151 of the Code for the purpose of evading or circumventing the conditions laid down therein. If the ground of challenge is a kind of fraud other than that contemplated in the said rule, which vitiated the proceeding altogether, recourse to section 151 of the Code will also not be ordinarily appropriate, as a properly framed suit under the general law will undoubtedly be a more appropriate remedy in such a case. 

 "In the present case the decretal suit property has been described in the decree as follows- 

 6. In our opinion the remedy of the 3rd party is available in a separate suit and the principle of law decided in 29 DLR (SC) 185 is applicable to the present case and the 3rd party may come to the picture in the execution case filed by a different person under Order 21 Rule 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure after eviction. The inherent power U/S. 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be invoked at the instance of 3rd party who is neither a party to the suit nor to the decree sought to be executed. Moreover he admittedly does not claim any interest in the suit holding but in a different holding and questions the identity of the suit land and has filed the application in apprehension of being dispossessed from his land. His such apprehension may be a cause of action for a separate suit for permanent injunction. Admittedly a separate suit had already been filed and a decree of permanent injunction has already been passed against the decree holder petitioner and so he cannot go to holding no. 339A. Mr. A.K.M. Shafiqur Rahman submits that if without ascertaining the location of holding no. 339 the decretal land, the decree holder dispossesses the 3rd party opposite party from holding no. 339A identifying it to be holding no.339 then multiplicity of legal proceeding shall be cropped up and the learned court below rightly passed the impugned order which has not prejudiced the decree holder, rather it would prevent the multiplicity of legal proceeding and would settle all the dispute once for all. We have already observed that the order of the executing court is harmless but every order must be passed with jurisdiction vested by law which is lacking in the present case. In this view of the matter the order cannot stand being passed without jurisdiction and is liable to be set aside. Before we part with the case we must observe that it is the duty of the executing court to give delivery of possession of the decretal property to the decree holder and he may pass necessary order if he finds that the ascertainment of the suit property by local investigation is necessary in order to see that the decree of the court is correctly executed although he cannot pass such order on an application of a 3rd party who has no locus standi in law at this stage before being evicted.
